manifest.title: Max Independent Set Remains NP-hard when Excluding a Planar Induced Minor

inputs.abstract:
We prove Theorem 5 of Bonnet and Chang: Maximum Independent Set is NP-hard
on graphs excluding the $5\times5$ grid as an induced minor. The reduction
from Max Cut constructs a graph $G_F$ in this class satisfying
$\alpha(G_F)=\operatorname{MaxCut}(F)+2\sum_{uv\in E(F),\,u<v}(v-u)$.
The formalization specifies induced minors, the construction, the structural
cycle obstruction, the independence-number identity, binary graph encodings,
and the polynomial-time reduction. It reuses the archive's definition of NP.

The result rules out the polynomial-time algorithms conjectured by
Dallard–Milanič–Štorgel and in the corresponding weighted induced-subgraph
generalization unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. The quasipolynomial-time
conjecture of Gartland–Lokshtanov and Korhonen would imply
$\mathrm{NP}\subseteq\mathrm{QP}$.

The Lean proofs include the cycle obstruction, the explicit independent-set
construction, and finite machines with polynomial running-time bounds for
both reductions. Max Cut hardness follows from the Cook–Levin circuit
compiler in lax-429075 through three-literal satisfiability, not-all-equal
satisfiability, and simple unweighted graph gadgets. All eight theorem and
lemma statements are proved. The ETH lower bound in Corollary 6 is outside
this submission.

concepts.title: Three mutually avoiding cycles
concepts.description:
A graph has three mutually avoiding cycles if it contains three vertex-disjoint,
pairwise nonadjacent cycles, and between any two there is a path avoiding
the closed neighborhood of the third. A walk suffices in the formal
definition, since deleting repeated portions gives a path with the same
avoidance property. This is the obstruction used in the proof of Claim 9.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Paths

/-!
---
title: Three mutually avoiding cycles
type: definition
---
A graph has three mutually avoiding cycles if it contains three vertex-disjoint,
pairwise nonadjacent cycles, and between any two there is a path avoiding
the closed neighborhood of the third. A walk suffices in the formal
definition, since deleting repeated portions gives a path with the same
avoidance property. This is the obstruction used in the proof of Claim 9.
-/

namespace Lax762056.AsteroidalCycles

def HasTriple {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (base : Fin 3 → V) (cycle : ∀ i, G.Walk (base i) (base i)),
    (∀ i, (cycle i).IsCycle) ∧
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ u ∈ (cycle i).support, ∀ v ∈ (cycle j).support,
      u ≠ v ∧ ¬ G.Adj u v) ∧
    (∀ i j k, i ≠ j → i ≠ k → j ≠ k →
      ∃ u ∈ (cycle i).support, ∃ v ∈ (cycle j).support,
        ∃ p : G.Walk u v, ∀ x ∈ p.support, ∀ y ∈ (cycle k).support,
          x ≠ y ∧ ¬ G.Adj x y)

end Lax762056.AsteroidalCycles

concepts.title: The intermediate graph of rows, columns, and sides
concepts.description:
For any row set $R$ and $c$ columns, the intermediate graph has vertices
$(r,j,s)\in R\times\{0,\ldots,c-1\}\times\{0,1\}$. Each column induces a
complete bipartite graph between its two sides. Within a row, every vertex
is adjacent to both vertices in each consecutive column. There are no other
edges. With $|R|=2|E(F)|$ and $c=2|V(F)|-1$ this is Figure 1 of the paper.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic

/-!
---
title: The intermediate graph of rows, columns, and sides
type: definition
---
For any row set $R$ and $c$ columns, the intermediate graph has vertices
$(r,j,s)\in R\times\{0,\ldots,c-1\}\times\{0,1\}$. Each column induces a
complete bipartite graph between its two sides. Within a row, every vertex
is adjacent to both vertices in each consecutive column. There are no other
edges. With $|R|=2|E(F)|$ and $c=2|V(F)|-1$ this is Figure 1 of the paper.
-/

namespace Lax762056.ColumnGraph

abbrev Vertex (R : Type*) (c : ℕ) := R × Fin c × Bool

def graph (R : Type*) (c : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Vertex R c) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun x y =>
    (x.2.1 = y.2.1 ∧ x.2.2 ≠ y.2.2) ∨
    (x.1 = y.1 ∧ (x.2.1.val + 1 = y.2.1.val ∨ y.2.1.val + 1 = x.2.1.val))

end Lax762056.ColumnGraph

concepts.title: The cycle obstruction to an induced minor
concepts.description:
Every cycle in an intermediate graph contains vertices on opposite sides of
one column. Their joint neighborhood contains that entire column. Consequently,
a graph with three mutually avoiding cycles cannot be an induced minor of
an intermediate graph. The $5\times5$ grid has such a triple (Figure 4).

These are the two structural ingredients of Claim 9. The obstruction is
stated for every intermediate graph, independently of the Max Cut instance.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax762056.AsteroidalCycles
import Lax762056.ColumnGraph
import Lax762056.Grid

/-!
---
title: The cycle obstruction to an induced minor
type: lemma
---
Every cycle in an intermediate graph contains vertices on opposite sides of
one column. Their joint neighborhood contains that entire column. Consequently,
a graph with three mutually avoiding cycles cannot be an induced minor of
an intermediate graph. The $5\times5$ grid has such a triple (Figure 4).

These are the two structural ingredients of Claim 9. The obstruction is
stated for every intermediate graph, independently of the Max Cut instance.
-/

namespace Lax762056.CycleObstruction

axiom excludes_triple (R W : Type*) (c : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph W)
    (hH : AsteroidalCycles.HasTriple H) :
  ¬ InducedMinors.IsInducedMinor H (ColumnGraph.graph R c)

axiom grid_has_triple : AsteroidalCycles.HasTriple Grid.grid

end Lax762056.CycleObstruction

concepts.title: Binary encoding of graph decision instances
concepts.description:
An instance is a finite simple graph on $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and a natural
threshold $k$. Its encoding is $1^n0$, followed by the $n^2$ adjacency-matrix
bits in row order, followed by $1^k0$. This includes the empty graph and
threshold zero, and uniquely specifies the entire instance.

Unary thresholds suffice for both problems: thresholds exceeding the number
of vertices for Independent Set, or the number of edges for Max Cut, can be
rejected immediately. On the remaining inputs this encoding is polynomially
equivalent to the usual binary-threshold encoding.

Polynomial time is measured in the length of this explicit binary encoding,
using the same finite Turing machines as the archive's definitions of P and
NP. Choosing truth values of the finitely many adjacency propositions below
does not posit an algorithm or a time bound; those are separate obligations.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique
import Mathlib.Data.List.FinRange
import Lax434930.PolynomialTime

/-!
---
title: Binary encoding of graph decision instances
type: definition
---
An instance is a finite simple graph on $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and a natural
threshold $k$. Its encoding is $1^n0$, followed by the $n^2$ adjacency-matrix
bits in row order, followed by $1^k0$. This includes the empty graph and
threshold zero, and uniquely specifies the entire instance.

Unary thresholds suffice for both problems: thresholds exceeding the number
of vertices for Independent Set, or the number of edges for Max Cut, can be
rejected immediately. On the remaining inputs this encoding is polynomially
equivalent to the usual binary-threshold encoding.

Polynomial time is measured in the length of this explicit binary encoding,
using the same finite Turing machines as the archive's definitions of P and
NP. Choosing truth values of the finitely many adjacency propositions below
does not posit an algorithm or a time bound; those are separate obligations.
-/

namespace Lax762056.GraphEncoding

open Lax434930.PolynomialTime

structure Instance where
  order : ℕ
  graph : SimpleGraph (Fin order)
  threshold : ℕ

def unary (n : ℕ) : Word := List.replicate n true ++ [false]

noncomputable def encode (I : Instance) : Word := by
  classical
  exact unary I.order ++
    (List.finRange I.order).flatMap (fun u =>
      (List.finRange I.order).map (fun v => decide (I.graph.Adj u v))) ++
    unary I.threshold

end Lax762056.GraphEncoding

concepts.title: Excluding the five-by-five grid as an induced minor
concepts.description:
The $5\times5$ grid has vertex set $\{0,\ldots,4\}^2$, with adjacency between
orthogonally consecutive positions. We use mathlib's Cartesian product of
two five-vertex paths. A graph belongs to the class in Theorem 5 precisely
when this grid is not its induced minor.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Hasse
import Lax762056.InducedMinors

/-!
---
title: Excluding the five-by-five grid as an induced minor
type: definition
---
The $5\times5$ grid has vertex set $\{0,\ldots,4\}^2$, with adjacency between
orthogonally consecutive positions. We use mathlib's Cartesian product of
two five-vertex paths. A graph belongs to the class in Theorem 5 precisely
when this grid is not its induced minor.
-/

namespace Lax762056.Grid

def grid : SimpleGraph (Fin 5 × Fin 5) :=
  (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 5).boxProd (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 5)

def ExcludesGrid {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ¬ InducedMinors.IsInducedMinor grid G

end Lax762056.Grid

concepts.title: The constructed graphs exclude the five-by-five grid
concepts.description:
Claim 9: the intermediate graph excludes the $5\times5$ grid as an induced
minor. Therefore every reduction graph $G_F$, being an induced subgraph of
an intermediate graph, also excludes this induced minor.

axiom intermediate (R : Type*) (c : ℕ) :
  Grid.ExcludesGrid (ColumnGraph.graph R c)

  Grid.ExcludesGrid (Reduction.graph F)

concepts.title: The independence number records the maximum cut
concepts.description:
Claim 10: for every finite simple graph $F$,
$\alpha(G_F)=\operatorname{MaxCut}(F)+b(F)$.
An independent set chooses at most one side in each column and so determines
a cut of $F$ (empty columns may be assigned either side). The two rows for
an edge $uv$ contribute at most $2(v-u)+1$ vertices, and at most $2(v-u)$
when its endpoints lie on the same side. Conversely, every cut realizes
the sum of these bounds. Independence number is mathlib's `SimpleGraph.indepNum`.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax762056.Reduction

/-!
---
title: The independence number records the maximum cut
type: lemma
---
Claim 10: for every finite simple graph $F$,
$\alpha(G_F)=\operatorname{MaxCut}(F)+b(F)$.
An independent set chooses at most one side in each column and so determines
a cut of $F$ (empty columns may be assigned either side). The two rows for
an edge $uv$ contribute at most $2(v-u)+1$ vertices, and at most $2(v-u)$
when its endpoints lie on the same side. Conversely, every cut realizes
the sum of these bounds. Independence number is mathlib's `SimpleGraph.indepNum`.
-/

namespace Lax762056.IndependenceIdentity

axiom identity {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) :
  (Reduction.graph F).indepNum = MaxCut.maxCut F + Reduction.offset F

end Lax762056.IndependenceIdentity

identity : ∀ {n : Nat} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
  Eq (Lax762056.Reduction.graph F).indepNum (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax762056.MaxCut.maxCut F) (Lax762056.Reduction.offset F))

concepts.title: Induced minors
concepts.description:
A graph $H$ is an induced minor of $G$ if its vertices have pairwise disjoint,
nonempty connected branch sets in $G$, and two distinct branch sets are joined
by an edge exactly when their vertices are adjacent in $H$. Thus edges between
retained branch sets cannot be deleted. For finite graphs this is the usual
definition by vertex deletions and edge contractions.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Connectivity.Connected

/-!
---
title: Induced minors
type: definition
---
A graph $H$ is an induced minor of $G$ if its vertices have pairwise disjoint,
nonempty connected branch sets in $G$, and two distinct branch sets are joined
by an edge exactly when their vertices are adjacent in $H$. Thus edges between
retained branch sets cannot be deleted. For finite graphs this is the usual
definition by vertex deletions and edge contractions.
-/

namespace Lax762056.InducedMinors

structure Model {W V : Type*} (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  branch : W → Set V
  connected : ∀ v, (G.induce (branch v)).Connected
  disjoint : ∀ u v, u ≠ v → Disjoint (branch u) (branch v)
  adjacent : ∀ u v, u ≠ v →
    (H.Adj u v ↔ ∃ x ∈ branch u, ∃ y ∈ branch v, G.Adj x y)

def IsInducedMinor {W V : Type*} (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (Model H G)

end Lax762056.InducedMinors

concepts.title: Maximum cuts
concepts.description:
For a graph $F$ on an ordered vertex set, each edge is represented once, by
its endpoints $u<v$. A cut is specified by a subset $S$ of vertices; its size
is the number of edges with exactly one endpoint in $S$. $\operatorname{MaxCut}(F)$
is the largest such size, with value zero for an edgeless graph.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax762056.GraphEncoding

/-!
---
title: Maximum cuts
type: definition
---
For a graph $F$ on an ordered vertex set, each edge is represented once, by
its endpoints $u<v$. A cut is specified by a subset $S$ of vertices; its size
is the number of edges with exactly one endpoint in $S$. $\operatorname{MaxCut}(F)$
is the largest such size, with value zero for an edgeless graph.
-/

namespace Lax762056.MaxCut

noncomputable def edges {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Finset (Fin n × Fin n) := by
  classical
  exact Finset.univ.filter fun e => e.1 < e.2 ∧ F.Adj e.1 e.2

noncomputable def cutSize {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact ((edges F).filter fun e => (e.1 ∈ S ∧ e.2 ∉ S) ∨ (e.1 ∉ S ∧ e.2 ∈ S)).card

noncomputable def maxCut {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).powerset.sup (cutSize F)

end Lax762056.MaxCut

concepts.title: NP-hardness of unweighted Max Cut
concepts.description:
Every language in NP reduces in polynomial time to the decision version of
Max Cut on finite simple unweighted graphs. For every binary input the
reduction outputs a well-formed graph and threshold, with cut size at least
the threshold exactly on yes-inputs.

The classical result is due to Garey, Johnson, and Stockmeyer (1976).
This is a prerequisite of Theorem 5. Its proof uses the Cook–Levin circuit
compiler from lax-429075, followed by the satisfiability-to-Max-Cut
reductions, each implemented by a polynomial-time machine. In particular, a
weighted or multigraph Max Cut hardness result alone does not discharge
this obligation.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax762056.MaxCut
import Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime

/-!
---
title: NP-hardness of unweighted Max Cut
type: lemma
---
Every language in NP reduces in polynomial time to the decision version of
Max Cut on finite simple unweighted graphs. For every binary input the
reduction outputs a well-formed graph and threshold, with cut size at least
the threshold exactly on yes-inputs.

The classical result is due to Garey, Johnson, and Stockmeyer (1976).
This is a prerequisite of Theorem 5. Its proof uses the Cook–Levin circuit
compiler from lax-429075, followed by the satisfiability-to-Max-Cut
reductions, each implemented by a polynomial-time machine. In particular, a
weighted or multigraph Max Cut hardness result alone does not discharge
this obligation.
-/

namespace Lax762056.MaxCutHard

open GraphEncoding MaxCut
open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime

axiom np_hard (A : Language) (hA : A ∈ NP) :
  ∃ f : Word → Instance,
    Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime id encode f) ∧
    ∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ (f x).threshold ≤ maxCut (f x).graph

end Lax762056.MaxCutHard

statements.signature:
np_hard : ∀ (A : Lax434930.PolynomialTime.Language),
  Set.instMembership.mem Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime.NP A →
    Exists fun f =>
      And (Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime id Lax762056.GraphEncoding.encode f))
        (∀ (x : Lax554803.PolynomialTime.Word),
          Iff (Set.instMembership.mem A x) (instLENat.le (f x).threshold (Lax762056.MaxCut.maxCut (f x).graph)))

concepts.title: The Bonnet–Chang reduction
concepts.description:
Order the vertices of $F$ as $0,\ldots,n-1$. For every edge $uv$ with $u<v$,
reserve rows $(uv,0)$ and $(uv,1)$ in an intermediate graph with $2n-1$
columns. Keep only columns from $2u$ through $2v$. In row $(uv,t)$ keep
only side $t$ at column $2u$ and side $1-t$ at column $2v$; keep both sides
at every intervening column. The resulting induced subgraph is $G_F$.

Column $2j$ here is column $2(j+1)-1$ in the paper's indexing. Labeling rows
by their edges avoids making an arbitrary choice of an edge ordering. The
additive offset is $b(F)=2\sum_{uv\in E(F),\,u<v}(v-u)$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax762056.ColumnGraph
import Lax762056.MaxCut

/-!
---
title: The Bonnet–Chang reduction
type: definition
---
Order the vertices of $F$ as $0,\ldots,n-1$. For every edge $uv$ with $u<v$,
reserve rows $(uv,0)$ and $(uv,1)$ in an intermediate graph with $2n-1$
columns. Keep only columns from $2u$ through $2v$. In row $(uv,t)$ keep
only side $t$ at column $2u$ and side $1-t$ at column $2v$; keep both sides
at every intervening column. The resulting induced subgraph is $G_F$.

Column $2j$ here is column $2(j+1)-1$ in the paper's indexing. Labeling rows
by their edges avoids making an arbitrary choice of an edge ordering. The
additive offset is $b(F)=2\sum_{uv\in E(F),\,u<v}(v-u)$.
-/

namespace Lax762056.Reduction

abbrev Edge {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) :=
  {e : Fin n × Fin n // e.1 < e.2 ∧ F.Adj e.1 e.2}

abbrev Row {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) := Edge F × Bool

abbrev Vertex {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) :=
  ColumnGraph.Vertex (Row F) (2 * n - 1)

def kept {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Set (Vertex F) :=
  {x | let u := x.1.1.val.1.val
       let v := x.1.1.val.2.val
       let t := x.1.2
       let j := x.2.1.val
       let s := x.2.2
       (j = 2 * u ∧ s = t) ∨
       (2 * u < j ∧ j < 2 * v) ∨
       (j = 2 * v ∧ s = !t)}

def graph {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : SimpleGraph (kept F) :=
  (ColumnGraph.graph (Row F) (2 * n - 1)).induce (kept F)

noncomputable def offset {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : ℕ :=
  2 * ∑ e ∈ MaxCut.edges F, (e.2.val - e.1.val)

end Lax762056.Reduction

concepts.title: The reduction can be computed in polynomial time
concepts.description:
There is a single polynomial time algorithm that, from the encoded instance
$(F,k)$, outputs an encoded graph isomorphic to $G_F$ with threshold $k+b(F)$.
Both input and output use the specified adjacency-matrix encoding. The graph
isomorphism permits the algorithm to enumerate the retained vertices in a
fixed order; it does not require a noncomputable relabeling to be executable.

The claim includes a finite Turing machine and a polynomial bound on its
actual computation time. A polynomial bound on the number of output vertices
alone is not sufficient to discharge it.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax762056.Reduction

/-!

title: The reduction can be computed in polynomial time
type: lemma
---
There is a single polynomial time algorithm that, from the encoded instance

Both input and output use the specified adjacency-matrix encoding. The graph
isomorphism permits the algorithm to enumerate the retained vertices in a
fixed order; it does not require a noncomputable relabeling to be executable.

The claim includes a finite Turing machine and a polynomial bound on its

namespace Lax762056.ReductionTime

open GraphEncoding

axiom polynomial_time :
  ∃ f : Instance → Instance,
    Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime encode encode f) ∧
    ∀ I, Nonempty ((f I).graph ≃g Reduction.graph I.graph) ∧
      (f I).threshold = I.threshold + Reduction.offset I.graph

end Lax762056.ReductionTime

statements.signature:
polynomial_time : Exists fun f =>
  And (Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime Lax762056.GraphEncoding.encode Lax762056.GraphEncoding.encode f))
    (∀ (I : Lax762056.GraphEncoding.Instance),
      And (Nonempty ((f I).graph.Iso (Lax762056.Reduction.graph I.graph)))
        (Eq (f I).threshold (instHAdd.hAdd I.threshold (Lax762056.Reduction.offset I.graph))))

concepts.title: MIS is NP-hard when excluding the five-by-five grid as an induced minor
concepts.description:
**Theorem 5 (Bonnet–Chang).** Maximum Independent Set is NP-hard on graphs
excluding the $5\times5$ grid as an induced minor.

Precisely, for every binary language $A$ in the archive's NP there is one
polynomial time reduction sending every word $x$ to a finite simple graph
$G_x$ and threshold $k_x$. Every $G_x$ excludes the grid as an induced minor,
and $x\in A$ if and only if $\alpha(G_x)\ge k_x$. The class restriction holds
on both yes- and no-inputs. The graph class need not be recognized by the
Independent Set algorithm.

This decision formulation also implies hardness of computing the maximum
independent-set size or an actual maximum independent set. The theorem has
no assumption that Max Cut is hard, no assumption about the reduction, and
no assumption separating complexity classes.

import Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime

/-!

title: MIS is NP-hard when excluding the five-by-five grid as an induced minor
type: theorem
---
**Theorem 5 (Bonnet–Chang).** Maximum Independent Set is NP-hard on graphs
excluding the $5\times5$ grid as an induced minor.

Precisely, for every binary language $A$ in the archive's NP there is one
polynomial time reduction sending every word $x$ to a finite simple graph
$G_x$ and threshold $k_x$. Every $G_x$ excludes the grid as an induced minor,
and $x\in A$ if and only if $\alpha(G_x)\ge k_x$. The class restriction holds
on both yes- and no-inputs. The graph class need not be recognized by the
Independent Set algorithm.

This decision formulation also implies hardness of computing the maximum
independent-set size or an actual maximum independent set. The theorem has
no assumption that Max Cut is hard, no assumption about the reduction, and
no assumption separating complexity classes.
-/

namespace Lax762056.Theorem5

open GraphEncoding
open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime

axiom np_hard (A : Language) (hA : A ∈ NP) :
  ∃ f : Word → Instance,
    Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime id encode f) ∧
    ∀ x, Grid.ExcludesGrid (f x).graph ∧
      (x ∈ A ↔ (f x).threshold ≤ (f x).graph.indepNum)

end Lax762056.Theorem5

  Set.instMembership.mem Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime.NP A →

proofs.description:
The three corner squares and boundary paths are explicit finite walks.
Their cycle, separation, and avoidance conditions are checked by reduction
in the Lean kernel.

Every independent set induces a cut, with at most the stated number of
vertices in each edge's two rows. Conversely, the explicit construction
from a maximum cut realizes the bound, including the additional vertex
for each crossing edge.
Apply the general obstruction to the explicit triple of cycles in the grid.

Compose the Cook–Levin circuit compiler with the finite machine constructing
the unweighted simple Max Cut gadgets. Unit and binary clauses are padded by
literal repetition; all edge occurrences receive distinct subdivision vertices.

Each cycle's branch sets contain opposite sides of a column. The three
columns are distinct. The middle column is contained in the middle cycle's
closed neighborhood and separates the other two cycles, contradicting their
avoiding path.

An induced-minor model in the retained graph lifts to its intermediate
graph simply by viewing its branch sets in the original vertex type.

A fixed finite stack machine enumerates the retained vertices, emits their
adjacency matrix, and adds the offset to the unary threshold. Its actual
running time is bounded using the verified bounded-query compiler.

Compose the proved Max Cut hardness reduction with the encoded construction,
then apply the induced-minor exclusion and independence-number identity.
The proof uses the published Cook–Levin circuit compiler and Tseitin
correctness; every graph and machine lemma specific to this submission is proved.
